proposals.title: Spatial Domain Detection
proposals.summary: This analysis would focus on identifying biologically meaningful domains within tissues by integrating expression data with spatial coordinates. The approach would involve constructing a neighborhood graph based on physical proximity, applying unsupervised clustering algorithms, and comparing clusters to known anatomical annotations. Emphasis would be on balancing transcriptomic signals with spatial continuity, discerning boundaries between distinct cell populations, and using spatial regularization techniques to improve domain detection robustness.

proposals.title: Spatial Trajectory Inference
proposals.summary: This analysis aims to capture developmental or disease progression trajectories across spatially organized regions. The workflow would integrate latent representations with spatial coordinates to infer potential migration paths or differentiation gradients. Graph-based trajectory inference methods would be enhanced by incorporating geospatial information, facilitating detection of transition states between spatially adjacent tissue regions. The goal is to preserve local neighborhood information while inferring global progression patterns.

proposals.title: Computational Batch Correction Using Spatial Anchoring
proposals.summary: Aiming to improve consistency across spatial transcriptomics platforms, this analysis would develop a batch correction pipeline that leverages spatial anchors. The strategy involves identifying regions with similar tissue architecture across batches, constructing shared spatial graphs, and applying correction algorithms that align latent spaces while preserving local spatial heterogeneity. Quantitative improvements would be evaluated using both spatial pattern preservation and reconstruction accuracy of expression profiles.

proposals.title: Spatial Noise Denoising and Signal Recovery
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on developing a denoising method that integrates spatial context. By modeling the gene expression signal as a combination of true biological variation and spatially correlated noise, the analysis would use graph convolutional neural networks or spatial smoothing techniques to reconcile dropout events and technical noise. This approach would be validated by assessing the quantitative recovery of obscured gene expression and improvement in downstream spatial analyses.

proposals.title: High-Resolution Embedding Learning
proposals.summary: Here, the objective is to learn a compact latent space that retains both gene expression patterns and fine-grained spatial structure. The analysis would involve dimensionality reduction methods that include explicit spatial regularization components to preserve neighborhood relationships. Techniques such as modified PCA or graph-based autoencoders would be explored, ensuring that the embeddings generalize across different resolutions, and enhance the detection of rare cell states in densely sampled regions.

proposals.title: Gene Expression Dropout Recovery in Spatial Context
proposals.summary: This analysis endeavors to recover missing gene expression data by exploiting spatial correlation and neighborhood gene expression patterns. The method would incorporate advanced imputation techniques that consider both cell-type specific expression and spatial adjacency, potentially using matrix factorization or deep learning frameworks that integrate spatial smoothing. The effectiveness of the imputation will be quantitatively tested against ground truth using simulation and experimental dropout patterns.

proposals.title: Coordinate-Informed Clustering of Transcriptomic Data
proposals.summary: The proposed analysis would integrate spatial coordinates directly into clustering workflows to improve the resolution of tissue dissection. Instead of applying clustering on expression data alone, this approach uses a joint optimization framework that simultaneously minimizes differences in gene expression and spatial distance. The method would involve developing cost functions that penalize large spatial leaps and erroneous grouping of distant but transcriptionally similar regions, thus preserving biological fidelity.

proposals.title: Spatial Neighborhood Graph Analysis
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on constructing and analyzing spatial neighborhood graphs to systematically assess relationships between adjacent tissue regions. By representing locations as nodes on a graph, with edges representing spatial proximity weighted by expression similarity, the study would deploy metrics from network theory to identify hubs and critical boundaries. Additionally, algorithms for community detection within the graph would be employed to refine tissue architecture maps, directly linking local interactions to global spatial organization.
